synthesis: Android documents a private virtual-display surface and foreground location-service behavior that make an app-owned screen-off renderer plausible; neither establishes continuous rendering on the target phone.
MapLibre provides rendering and offline-region APIs, while map-data rights, coverage, attribution, availability and download limits are controlled by a separate provider.

The selected OpenFreeMap usage requires an identifying User-Agent, current per-pack limits, visible attribution and a feasibility gate if the Android SDK cannot bound a pack before it exceeds those limits.
H.264/RTP defaults and joystick semantics are community observations. The default video profile, K1G behavior and input mapping remain unverified against the owner’s FOTA 11.63 TFT.
Route geometry and live GPS can remain on-device; map preparation sends requests for the selected area to the provider.

The debug APK is installed on the iQOO I2405, has joined the owner-reported Tripper Wi-Fi after the owner entered its passphrase on-device, and reports the phone-side renderer stream active; the owner reported the renderer test pattern visible on the TFT. Separately, the owner confirmed the Royal Enfield full-map route remained visible during one unlocked display-off trial; this did not validate MirrorDash's Shizuku binder path or the new app-owned renderer.
contradictions: OpenDash maps observed joystick codes to zoom actions while BetterDash maps them to directional UI navigation; only parked observation on the target bike can resolve the conflict.
Android documents virtual-display and foreground-service behavior, but no reviewed source proves continuous MapLibre rendering to the TFT when this OEM phone is screen-off or locked.
limitations: No raw TFT packet capture or independent TFT image capture, joystick trial, offline-region download, screen-off/lock test or thermal measurement has been performed for the new app-owned architecture; the owner reported the renderer test pattern visible.

MapLibre offline API status does not expose a total required-byte estimate before region download completion; implementation must prove it can remain within provider terms or stop provider integration.
Provider terms, endpoint availability and map coverage can change and must be rechecked before release.
Context.dev tools were unavailable during earlier research; primary Android/MapLibre documentation and source repository references were used.
license_and_redistribution_constraints: OpenMotoDash and BetterDash are Apache-2.0 repositories; protocol reference does not require copying code, and any copied source must retain applicable notices.
MapLibre code and provider map data have separate licenses and terms. Preserve OpenStreetMap and any additional source attribution in the app.
OpenFreeMap terms and service limits must be followed; do not evade limits by dividing a download.

confidence.rationale: Android and MapLibre APIs are documented. Target renderer behavior, provider cap enforcement and Tripper FOTA 11.63 interoperability are unverified.

review_triggers: Recheck Android location, foreground-service, DisplayManager and Doze requirements when target SDK or Android support changes.
Recheck MapLibre artifacts and offline API behavior before implementation if the plan is run later.
Recheck OpenFreeMap terms, service availability, endpoint and style before release.
Replace community protocol and joystick assumptions with parked-device evidence before asserting FOTA 11.63 compatibility.
Reassess the private VirtualDisplay renderer if it freezes, loses frames or fails when the phone is screen-off or locked.
